news.title: ‘Edward E. Boccia: Painter of Nightmares and Dreams’
news.summary_en: A new book, “Edward E. Boccia: Painter of Nightmares and Dreams,” revisits the life and work of the St. Louis painter, who taught at WashU from 1951 to 1986.

news.title: Freezing out tumors
news.summary_en: A WashU Medicine radiologist is on a mission to expand a minimally invasive procedure called cryoablation as a safe option for patients.

news.title: Strong reading skills may help teens resist misinformation
news.summary_en: Students with stronger reading skills are better able to spot misinformation online — and that may be especially important for teenagers from disadvantaged backgrounds, according to a new study from the Brown School.

news.title: WashU Leadership Week expands programming, partnerships
news.summary_en: WashU Leadership Week, hosted by the Bauer Leaders Academy, offers workshops and panel discussions for students, faculty and staff. Programming includes leadership development sessions for faculty and staff plus the annual “She Leads” Symposium.

news.title: New building blocks expand functions of photonic chips
news.summary_en: McKelvey Engineering researchers Sang-Hoon Bae and Lan Yang collaborated to establish a framework for heterogeneous integrated photonic chips, enabling multiple functions on a single chip with greater freedom to combine materials and design devices.

news.title: ‘It’s up to us to be advocates, healers, make connections’
news.summary_en: First-year WashU Medicine MD and MD/PhD students received their white coats at a ceremony Oct. 2. Other ceremonies recognized incoming students studying physical therapy, occupational therapy and audiology.

news.title: WashU research helped shape important step with Trump Accounts
news.summary_en: Research from the WashU Brown School’s Center for Social Development helped lay the groundwork for a major change to the federal government’s new Trump Accounts program: automatic account creation for eligible children, which the administration announced Sept. 29.

news.title: Amazon’s smart glasses raise privacy concerns
news.summary_en: Amazon’s introduction of smart glasses for its delivery drivers raises significant questions about privacy, workplace surveillance and the normalization of continuously recording technology, says  WashU Law professor Neil Richards.

news.title: Iconic illustrator Mary Engelbreit donates collection to WashU Libraries
news.summary_en: Beloved illustrator Mary Engelbreit has donated 120 original illustrations and related materials to WashU Libraries. The collection highlights her whimsical style, business acumen and activism and will support research, teaching and a public exhibition planned for July.
